evidence: The archived two funded-risk candidates are rejected, not rerun. All 144 manifest files, source tree and dependencies were verified. Reconstructing actual pre-2026 filled inventory reproduces every close target within 1.12e-16 in all six saved selection replays. hypothesis: Keep the risk-required economic inventory ceiling distinct from the conservatively lot-rounded request. This may prevent recursive involuntary liquidation and purchase freezes without relaxing any actual loss budget, warning, stop, concentration limit or unresolved economic obligation.
fixed_parent: Use the original funded-risk 10% risk budget, two positions, same boolean cushion alternatives, unchanged permanent actual-NAV peak, 1% exploration-risk floor when enabled, original warning-driven new-commitment authority, stops, selection, sizing, recovery and fees. No forecast fit, threshold search or new securities.
intent: Immediately before lot rounding, capture the required desired economic units. Latch that unrounded ceiling, or a stricter previous outstanding economic ceiling. Emit the same conservatively rounded executable declaration as the parent. An actual partial fill above the economic ceiling remains pending and blocks all purchases; a blocked sale remains pending. An actual fill at or below the economic ceiling satisfies it even if the fill differs from the rounding padding. New risk, stop or concentration violations may impose a stricter ceiling. No clearance based solely on a rebound, restored authority, small size, elapsed time, expected proceeds or a numerical tolerance wider than the existing unit tolerance. Full exits still require actual zero inventory.
implementation: Add one explicit behavior-preserving latch hook to support_budget.Owner. Its default stores the same rounded targets as before. The separately registered funded_intent.Owner changes only that latch to retain the economic ceiling. Preserve support_budget and funded_risk historical decisions exactly through actual-observation equivalence checks. Bind both parent implementations and contracts in the finite runner identity.
